summary: The extension's screen-control agent genuinely works at the layer that matters mechanically: a ref-based click validates server-side, resolves against the live DOM in a real Chromium and lands on the correct element; click -> focus -> type -> Enter fills and submits a form. All of that was verified by driving the extension's OWN executor on a page this agent owns, with no owner session and no paid model call. The product's real weakness is what happens when grounding fails. An unresolved ref is silently skipped by the popup executor and then reported to the user as 'N action(s) executed', while the second executor (agent_mode.js) aborts the whole burst on the identical input with a CDP 'Invalid parameters' error. Worse, the server's search fallback re-introduced a blind viewport-centre click: on a page with no field it clicks a guessed point while the reply claims a search. The repo's own tests forbid exactly this and currently fail on it (2 red in test_browser_action_hardening.py). Three user-facing claims are also false against the shipped code: credentials/OTP/cards/downloads are 'hard-blocked in every mode' (agent_mode.js:1111-1129 makes them RISKY, so YOLO runs them); 'Execute ships OFF' (popup.js:33 EXECUTE_DEFAULT=true, measured ON on a fresh profile); and 'learning platforms are read-only' (no such guard exists). Headline fix: keep x/y as a fallback on ref ops (screen_vision._validate_op:419-429), make both executors report an unresolved target instead of counting it as run, and delete the centre-of-viewport search heuristic.

findings.title: Search fallback blind-clicks the viewport centre-top, and the tests that forbid it are red
findings.symptom: On a page with no input field, 'search for photosynthesis' still moves the cursor and clicks a guessed point near the top-centre of the page while the reply says it is searching. The user sees an unexplained cursor movement and a wrong click.
findings.root_cause: routes_extension.py:798-802 reintroduces a viewport-centre-top heuristic that fires whenever no target was found by the measured-element list (762-790) or the vision parse (793-796). It contradicts the contract asserted by server/tests/test_browser_action_hardening.py:94-136, and it is reachable on the normal path: _resolve_fallback_control_actions (1043-1083) calls _search_burst whenever the model's control block is absent or invalid and the user text contains search/click/type keywords (1067, 1076-1083).
evidence: server/routes_extension.py:798-802 - target = {'x': vw // 2, 'y': min(130, max(40, vh // 6))}

measured: .venv/bin/python -m pytest server/tests/test_browser_action_hardening.py -q -> 2 failed, 111 passed (test_search_burst_does_nothing_when_no_field_is_on_screen; test_search_burst_target_is_kept_inside_the_captured_frame)

measured: _search_burst('photosynthesis', {'width':1280,'height':800}) -> [{'op':'move','x':640,'y':130},{'op':'click','x':640,'y':130,'button':'left'},{'op':'type','text':'photosynthesis','clear':True},{'op':'key','key':'Enter','modifiers':[]}]
server/routes_extension.py:1097 - the honest alternative already exists: reason 'no_target' -> 'I couldn't find that field on the current screen, so I didn't click anywhere.'
findings.impact: A wrong click on the user's screen plus a false claim of success - the exact trust failure this product cannot afford, and a visible-action safety issue.

findings.title: An unresolved ref is silently skipped and then reported as an executed action (popup executor)
findings.symptom: The popup prints 'Drove <tab> - N action(s) executed' even when one of those actions never happened. The page is unchanged and the user has no way to tell.
findings.root_cause: popup.js driveActionsInTab resolves refs at 2831, then dispatches in an if/else-if chain that every branch gates on op.x/op.y being defined (2871, 2875, 2892, 2909, 2961, 3000). An op with neither coordinates nor text matches nothing and there is no else branch, so it is dropped in silence; 3019 then returns ran: actions.length and 3087 prints the success line. resolveActionRefs leaves an unmatched ref untouched (element_registry.js:380-393) and refs are positional indices (element_registry.js:145), so this also fires after any DOM change between capture and dispatch - and then the ref can point at the wrong element rather than merely missing.
evidence: measured in a real Chromium (Playwright persistent context, channel chromium, --load-extension extension/): driveActionsInTab(tab, [{'op':'click','ref':9999}]) -> {'status':'ok','ran':1,'label':'H8 capability probe'} and document.getElementById('qs').value === '' (unchanged)
extension/popup.js:3019 - return { status: 'ok', ran: actions.length, ... }
extension/popup.js:3084-3090 - 'Drove ... - ${n} action(s) executed'
extension/element_registry.js:380-383 - if (hit) return Object.assign({}, op, {x, y}); otherwise the op falls through unchanged
findings.impact: False success reporting on the agent's core capability, and it hides grounding failures so the operator cannot measure how often the agent actually acts.

findings.title: The same unresolved ref aborts the whole burst in the Agent Mode executor
findings.symptom: From Agent Mode a stale ref kills the remaining actions in the burst; the log shows 'drive burst failed' and nothing explains that one target was simply not found.
findings.root_cause: agent_mode.js:915-921 maps coordinates unconditionally: to = pt(op.x ?? op.toX, op.y ?? op.toY). With a ref-only op the coordinate is undefined, so to = {x:NaN,y:NaN}; mouseEvent (880-893) does Math.round(NaN), which serialises to null, and CDP rejects the whole call; runActions' catch (1333-1334) then abandons the rest of the list.
evidence: extension/agent_mode.js:919 - const pt = (x, y) => ({ x: x * sx, y: y * sy }) applied to an undefined op.x
measured: JSON.stringify({x:Math.round(undefined),y:Math.round(undefined)}) -> {"x":null,"y":null}

measured in a real Chromium: chrome.debugger.sendCommand(Input.dispatchMouseEvent, {type:'mousePressed',x:NaN,...}) throws {"code":-32602,"data":"Failed to deserialize params.x - BINDINGS: mandatory field missing","message":"Invalid parameters"}
findings.impact: One stale ref costs the user the entire rest of the burst - a partial task that looks like a total failure, with the working actions dropped.

findings.title: Submission-facing copy claims hard-blocked credentials/downloads and read-only LMS; the code runs them in YOLO
findings.symptom: A Chrome Web Store reviewer, or a user reading the listing, is told signing-in fields, one-time codes, card numbers and downloads are blocked in every mode, and that learning platforms are read-only. Neither is true.
findings.root_cause: The 09-08 operator ruling made credential/OTP/card/download actions RISKY instead of forbidden (agent_mode.js:1103-1113); actionApproved asks only in Manual/Automatic and returns true unconditionally for YOLO (1227-1228). The CWS review document was not updated in those places.
evidence: extension/CWS_APPROVAL_REVIEW.md:118 - store listing: 'Signing-in fields, one-time codes, card numbers, and file downloads are hard-blocked in every mode'
extension/CWS_APPROVAL_REVIEW.md:131 - permission justification: 'Credential/OTP/card fields, downloads, and learning platforms are hard-blocked in every mode'
extension/CWS_APPROVAL_REVIEW.md:144 - 'hard blocks (credentials/OTP/cards/downloads) apply in every mode'
extension/agent_mode.js:1111-1113 - RISKY_CORES = {credential, credential-adjacent, download, destructive, submit, leaving}
extension/agent_mode.js:1227-1228 - auto+non-risky, or yolo: return true (no prompt)
extension/agent_mode.js:21-23 - stale header comment still says these are 'blocked in every mode'
grep -rn 'read-only|readOnly|readonly' extension/*.js -> only background.js:1032 (unrelated); instructure.com is in manifest.json host_permissions
findings.impact: A false safety claim in a store submission is a policy/misrepresentation risk and an informed-consent failure: a YOLO user is told credentials are untouchable and then the agent types into them.

findings.title: Execute ships ON in the popup while every document and the other surface say OFF
findings.symptom: On a fresh install the popup shows Execute already switched on, with no user action. Opening Agent Mode for the same account shows it off. The two surfaces disagree about the same switch.
findings.root_cause: popup.js:33 sets EXECUTE_DEFAULT = true and applies it whenever the storage key is absent (340, 360, 582, 3171, 3200), while agent_mode.js:60 sets EXECUTE_DEFAULT = false and popup.html:343 marks the input aria-checked="false". Nothing writes the key on first run, so both defaults are live at once.
evidence: measured on a fresh Playwright profile with the unpacked extension: #toggleExecute.checked === true, aria-checked === 'true', and chrome.storage.local returned only {helpotron_agent_effort, helpotron_agent_model, helpotron_agent_model_tier, update_available} - no helpotron_chat_execute
extension/popup.js:33 - const EXECUTE_DEFAULT = true; extension/agent_mode.js:60 - const EXECUTE_DEFAULT = false
extension/DESIGN-UX.md:165-166,178 - 'helpotron_chat_execute (default **false**)'
extension/CWS_APPROVAL_REVIEW.md:42,131 - 'Execute ... default OFF', 'it ships OFF'
extension/popup.js:3221 sends execute: !!executeOn; extension/agent_mode.js:1434 sends execute: state.execute - opposite values for the same unset key
findings.impact: The documented safety default is not the shipped default on the primary surface, and the same switch silently means two different things depending on which page the user opened.

findings.title: Unguarded int() on client-supplied element coordinates can 500 the agent turn
findings.symptom: A single element in the client's element list with a non-numeric x/y turns an agent message into an error instead of an action.
findings.root_cause: routes_extension.py accepts elements as List[Dict[str, Any]] (471-475) with no per-item validation, and _search_burst/_click_burst call int() on those dict values directly at 768, 787-788, 827, 837, 885, 907 and 943 with no try/except. _render_live_elements does it correctly (555-558).
evidence: measured: _search_burst('photosynthesis', {'width':1280,'height':800}, elements=[{'name':'Submit','role':'button','x':'z','y':3}]) -> ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'z'
measured: the same call with elements=[None, 5, 'x'] -> AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'
server/routes_extension.py:768 - cx, cy = int(el.get('x', 0)), int(el.get('y', 0))
server/routes_extension.py:555-558 - the guarded pattern that should be used everywhere
findings.impact: Any authenticated client can break its own agent turn on the fallback path; the user sees a failed request rather than an honest 'no target'.

findings.title: Only the first 150 measured elements are ref-addressable though 5000 are accepted
findings.symptom: On dense pages the model is told to prefer refs but sees at most 150 of the page's controls, so the elements it needs often have no ref and it falls back to pixel estimates.
findings.root_cause: _render_live_elements is called with limit=150 (routes_extension.py:1415) while ExtensionChatRequest.elements accepts 5000 (471-475) and element_registry.js:42 collects 5000. Refs are sequential indices (element_registry.js:145), so the visible window is exactly refs 0..149.
evidence: server/routes_extension.py:1415 - live_elements = _render_live_elements(payload.elements, limit=150)
server/routes_extension.py:550 - for el in (elements or [])[:limit]
extension/element_registry.js:42 - MAX_INTERACTIVE_ELEMENTS = 5000
findings.impact: Degrades grounding exactly where the ref path was built to help; the model silently reverts to estimated coordinates on the pages that most need precision.

Leave the existing `if not target: return []` at 804-805. The caller already turns an empty burst into reason 'no_target' (routes_extension.py:1083) with the honest message at 1097.
fixes.risk: Fewer actions on pages where the agent previously guessed and was occasionally right; the reply will say it could not find the field. That is the documented contract (test_browser_action_hardening.py:115-125).
fixes.verify: cd /home/roni/Roni_workspace/helpotron && .venv/bin/python -m pytest server/tests/test_browser_action_hardening.py -q — must go from '2 failed' to '0 failed'. (2) Count dispatched ops, not planned ones: declare `let dispatched = 0;` before the loop at 2860, increment it once per action whose branch actually ran, and change line 3019 to `return { status: 'ok', ran: dispatched, planned: actions.length, label, unseen: drivingUnseen };`. (3) Report the gap: at 3079 replace `const n = actions.length;` with `const n = done[0].ran; const planned = actions.length;` and append ` (${planned - n} target(s) not found)` to the status strings at 3084-3090 whenever planned > n.

fixes.change: Keep the model's coordinates as a fallback when a ref is present, so a stale ref is not a dead op. For 'move'/'dblclick': compute xy = _clamp_coords(op, viewport) first, then when ref is not None return {'op': name, 'ref': ref, 'x': xy[0], 'y': xy[1]} if xy else {'op': name, 'ref': ref}. For 'click' (419-429): ref = _ref_of(op); xy = _clamp_coords(op, viewport); if ref is not None: out = {'op': 'click', 'ref': ref, 'button': button}; if xy: out['x'], out['y'] = xy; return out. resolveActionRefs already overwrites x/y from the resolved element (element_registry.js:382), so a resolving ref still wins.
fixes.risk: A ref that resolves to the WRONG element (positional drift) still overrides x/y - that behaviour already exists today via Object.assign, so this does not widen it; it only adds a fallback when the ref misses entirely.
fixes.verify: .venv/bin/python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.'); from server.screen_vision import _validate_op; print(_validate_op({'op':'click','ref':4,'x':10,'y':20}, {'width':1280,'height':800}))" — must contain both ref 4 and x=10,y=20. Also assert a ref-only op still validates, and run .venv/bin/python -m pytest server/tests/test_extension_ref_actions.py -q (must stay green).

fixes.change: Refuse to dispatch a non-finite coordinate. After `const to = pt(op.x ?? op.toX, op.y ?? op.toY);` insert: `if ((op.op === 'move' || op.op === 'click' || op.op === 'dblclick' || op.op === 'drag') && (!Number.isFinite(to.x) || !Number.isFinite(to.y))) { pushLog('warn', 'skipped (unresolved target): ' + JSON.stringify(op)); return false; }`. Returning false does not abort the loop: runActions only breaks on `ok === false && state.pendingStop` (agent_mode.js:1323).
fixes.risk: An action with a genuinely missing target is now skipped and logged instead of destroying the burst; the log gains a new warn line.

verification_plan: Independent reviewer checklist for this track: (1) server-side op contract — run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest server/tests/test_extension_ref_actions.py server/tests/test_browser_action_hardening.py server/tests/test_extension_screen_feed.py server/tests/test_extension_live_elements.py server/tests/test_screen_control_targeting.py -q` from the repo root; before any fix this must show exactly 2 failed (both in test_browser_action_hardening.py, both _search_burst), after H8-X1 it must be 0 failed. (2) The five direct-execution probes: _validate_op with a ref-only click, with ref+xy, with out-of-range coords, with an invalid key, and _harden_actions with 16 ops; the expected outputs are recorded in the scorecard evidence strings above and can be reproduced in one python -c. (3) The end-to-end capability probe: serve any local page on 127.0.0.1 (which is in host_permissions), launch Playwright from web/ with `channel:'chromium'`, a persistent context and `--load-extension=extension/`, open popup.html as a page, then call driveActionsInTab(tab, actions, {activeTab: tab}) with (a) [{'op':'click','ref':0}] and assert the page reacts, (b) [{'op':'click','ref':9999}] and assert the returned ran matches what the DOM shows (this is the assertion that currently fails the product's honesty claim). (4) The claims audit: grep the store-facing text for 'hard-blocked' and 'read-only' and check each against agent_mode.js:1111-1129 and 1227-1228; and load a fresh profile to check the Execute toggle default against DESIGN-UX.md:178. (5) Not covered by this track and still owed: a live vision turn through the real OpenRouter lane (one paid call with a real screenshot), and a real tabCapture run (needs a user gesture) to confirm the agent_mode frame->CSS rescale on a display with devicePixelRatio != 1.

external_research.what: WebArena (Zhou et al., ICLR 2024) — 812 execution-scored browser tasks across self-hosted web apps; human baseline 78.24%, best agents ~60-70%
external_research.why: Calibrates what 'good' looks like for a browser agent: even frontier systems fail roughly a third of realistic multi-step tasks, so any product claiming reliable homework automation should publish its own grounding failure rate rather than assert success. Also the reason a per-step miss must be counted and reported (H8-F2/F3).

external_research.what: OSWorld (Xie et al., NeurIPS 2024) — 369 real desktop tasks, 1920x1080 screenshots, free-form mouse/keyboard; human baseline ~72.4%, best agents 60-76% in 2025
external_research.why: The canonical measurement that GUI grounding (pixels -> the right element) is the dominant failure mode for exactly the capability this product sells. It is the justification for investing in the measured DOM element registry (element_registry.js) over vision-estimated coordinates.

external_research.what: Set-of-Mark prompting (Yang et al., 2023) — overlay numbered marks on interactive elements so a vision model can refer to them by id instead of estimating pixels
external_research.why: This is the published form of the SoM overlay already implemented in element_registry.js:195-261. The paper is the evidence that the ref-based grounding path (now verified working end to end) is the right architecture, and that the refs must be the ones the model is actually shown.
external_research.license: n/a (research paper; code at github.com/microsoft/SoM - check repo licence before reuse)

external_research.what: 'An Illusion of Progress? Assessing the Current State of Web Agents' (Xue et al., COLM 2025) — shows WebVoyager overstates ability (a search-only agent solves up to 51% of tasks; Browser Use self-reports 89% there but scores 8.1% on hard Online-Mind2Web tasks)
external_research.why: The methodological rule this track applied to the product: a benchmark or claim that cannot be independently reproduced is not evidence. It is also why this report insists on measured probes and marks vision as UNVERIFIED rather than assuming it works.

open_questions: Does the vision lane actually describe the screen usefully? Requires one paid OpenRouter call (analyze_screen_image with a real JPEG). Not made here to respect the no-paid-loop instruction; the code path and its fail-closed fallback are verified, the output quality is not.

Does the agent_mode (tabCapture) path put frame coordinates and CSS coordinates in the same space on a display with devicePixelRatio != 1? The arithmetic (agent_mode.js:857-871, 1450-1459) is self-consistent but untested because tabCapture.getMediaStreamId needs a real user gesture. A single manual run on a 2x display, clicking a known element and checking where the cursor lands, settles it.

How often does a ref actually go stale in practice? The failure requires a DOM change between capture and dispatch. An instrumented run that logs every unresolvable ref (after H8-X2/X4) would turn this from a design risk into a measured rate.

In one headless harness state Page.captureScreenshot returned 1280x633 for a 1280x720 viewport, which normalizeFrame then stretched to 720; a follow-up measurement across 600/720/1000 viewport heights returned exact sizes, so it is attributed to headless background-tab surface behaviour. If it reproduces on a real display it becomes a genuine vertical-offset bug and should move to a finding.

Does the popup Chat surface still exist intentionally? DESIGN-UX.md:240-241 says the popup mini-chat was removed in favour of Agent Mode, but popup.js:3127-3337 still implements a full chat form with its own send path and executor. Two chat surfaces with two executors is the root of H8-F2 vs H8-F3 diverging; a decision on which one is the product is needed before the fixes are finalised.
